propositions: An acceptance criterion tagged [operator-attested] citing exact repository paths/symbols (code-verifiable evidence) was incorrectly accepted at close despite layered guards that should have rejected it.
The evidence-kind routing criterion failed to block a tagged AC with inline repository path citations; the LLM judgment missed the laundering pattern and no deterministic backstop existed.

The det_measurement_provenance detector identified missing provenance continuation lines on tagged ACs but wired them as advisory (p6_ac_quality) rather than blocking, allowing the defect to pass review.

A deterministic, pre-LLM close-path guard (ensure_attested_items_valid + det_attestation_launder) now rejects tagged ACs containing repository path/symbol citations unless they declare external evidence via provenance lines.

The guard distinguishes test-shaped citations (tests/ paths, test_* symbols, pytest nodes) which always fire, from other repo citations which fire only when preceded by evidence-introducing keywords on the same line.
Mixed-evidence ACs (both repo-verifiable and external outcomes cited) are now blocked with coaching to split into separate untagged and tagged criteria.
